purpose: Source atlas for a future native Substack adapter; not consumed by shipped runtime.
qualification: Anonymous desktop HTTP probes, plus existing production JVM NetworkGateway/RssSources checks. No source cookies, keys or page JavaScript execution. Live Tor and physical-phone availability not qualified. Status is target- and time-specific.
latencyCaveat: Single development-laptop observations, not a benchmark; HTTP probe timings include a 350 ms pacing delay and may include per-host queue time.

routes.notes: 20 dated entries on each sampled publication; custom-domain alias redirected to the same publisher. Feed is a recent window, not full history. Existing RSS reader can consume it.

Two 3-entry archive pages had six distinct IDs; three publication hosts succeeded. Publication-scoped search returned a different matching candidate set. Full-text relevance was not exhaustively evaluated.
Alternate list endpoint; do not infer complete bodies or reliable pagination from this first-page probe.
Free samples had substantial matching bodies. A paid-only sample exposed a partial body, not a full paid article. Preserve audience and extraction completeness.
HTTP acquisition and static parsing only; never execute page scripts. Strictly decode embedded JSON rather than evaluating assignments.

Same public profile identity through three tested hosts. These share Substack infrastructure. Sample profile exceeded 1 MB; project and cache only needed public fields, honor subscriptionsTruncated and avoid retaining incidental account timestamps.
Two pages of 12 had 24 distinct entity keys. Preserve activity type and original publication date separately from restack time.
Validate item.comment.id against the selected Note, retain parent relationships and stable user IDs.

First sample had eight branches, moreBranches=1 and a nextCursor. Following it, including comment_id, repeated all eight branch IDs. Pagination is not qualified; stop on zero novel IDs and retain partial coverage.
Static note/embed responses contain the note presentation. Embed is not a complete discussion or publication feed.

Four real comments on the custom-domain sample, with nested children fields. Other samples had none. Best-first and newest-first probes returned the same four descending dates; sort enforcement and large-thread completeness remain unqualified.
Separate reader-thread representation returned four branches, moreBranches=0 and no nextCursor for one small discussion. Not proof of complete large discussions.
Public query returned 20 results and a more flag despite limit=3. Do not trust a requested result limit; locally bound parsing. This does not establish global article or Notes search.
One recommendation in the sample, with recommended publication identity and domain. Recommendation is not proof of common ownership.
One publicly listed publication user in the sample. Not a reader/follower graph or complete ownership proof.
Eight tested hosts returned 20-entry RSS. Upstream adapter reads publication /feed; it adds no Notes or paid access. The balancer may share downstream operators with other entries.
Three tested hosts returned 20-entry Atom. Several listed hosts have this bridge disabled. Optional server-configured SID support is not an accountless phone capability.
Matched article and publication IDs; directory sample returned three items. Directory and metadata include excerpts, not full article bodies.

First response is a short-lived signed download URL, not Markdown. Download returned 20,909 characters matching 35/38 sampled body passages. Keep title/canonical identity from metadata, validate HTTPS destination, do not persist signed query credentials.

Read-only conversion POST {url,format:md,platform:substack,browserCapture:false}, no session field or cookies. JSON included title and 21,163-character Markdown matching 35/38 body passages. Credentialed paid mode is separate and excluded.
Served selected article HTML with 38/38 sampled body passages; client-side reader cleanup can be reimplemented locally. Broad paywall marketing is not proof of full paid access.
Served article HTML at the proxy URL without HTTP redirect; 38/38 sampled body passages matched. Operator and durability not established. Revalidate before enabling.
Three article metadata rows; code tries /api/v1/posts then /api/v1/archive and truncates excerpts to 240 characters. Reject its random fallback IDs and invented Unknown dates. Not a full-text route.
Source hardcodes ryanhockstein.substack.com/feed. Three rows returned. Only applicable to that publication; do not generalize to arbitrary publishers.
Accept: application/json returned data.url/title/content; exact selected URL and 35/38 sampled body passages matched. About 15.8 seconds in one desktop request; reserve for fallback. May be cached.

Anonymous GET returned ok/requested_url/results.markdown/status_code. Matched 35/38 body passages, but included navigation/subscribe text; still apply local content cleaning. Service documents up to 24-hour cached responses.
Read-only conversion POST {url}; JSON url/title/markdown matched selected article and 35/38 body passages. No browser session. Public web endpoint, not a stability guarantee.
Returned four feed entries, not the original twenty. Useful bounded fallback with explicit coverage; cannot claim catch-up completion from this sample.

Exact-URL index located a 20261022200555 capture; replay matched all 38 sampled body passages. Capture date is an archive observation, not a new post publication date. Existing archive engine can reuse this path.
Index reachable but zero captures for the sampled article; no Substack replay qualified. Keep target miss distinct from provider outage.

Documents Notes/replies/restacks, but selected handle returned an HTML feed-creation page and publication request hit 429. Do not repeatedly retry or count HTML as feed. A separately supplied, verified feed could be supported later.

Public page offers three anonymous conversions per day. Script exposes generation/download POSTs; no conversion requested in this audit. Optional user-directed export lead, not a background polling source.
Observed 403, 502, 522 and 403 respectively. These are shared-origin transport/format relays, not independent archives; do not add to healthy pool.

Old Glitch root redirects to migrated site; project supplies share metadata plus navigation, not independent article text. selcukcihan documents the same pattern. Preserve as incoming-link recognition references.

Found Superstack, substack-edgelord, Data Mine block adapter and author-configured AEO reverse proxies. Match actual publication/post IDs or canonical declarations; no arbitrary-publisher hosted service established.

Scraper repo includes publication/feed metadata and custom domains, but live directory page returned 403. Treat its older snapshots as leads requiring live identity/feed checks. Do not ship a giant static directory or confuse subscriber estimates with current facts.
Publisher API wrapper requires a publication API key; this is not an anonymous source for arbitrary creators. No key or private analytics requested.
